# AGENTS.java.md — Java

Additive to `../AGENTS.md`. Applies to every `.java` file. Spring Boot rules are
in `AGENTS.spring.md`.

## Build and check

```bash
./gradlew spotlessCheck test                # Gradle
./mvnw -B -ntp spotless:check verify        # Maven
```

Formatting is Spotless (google-java-format). Run `spotlessApply` before you push.

## Java rules

- Records for data carriers. Sealed interfaces for closed hierarchies, and on
  Java 21+ an exhaustive pattern-matching `switch` over them.
- `var` only when the type is obvious from the right-hand side.
- No `null` from public methods. Return `Optional<T>` for a value that may be
  absent and an empty collection for "none". Never `Optional` as a field or
  parameter.
- Immutable by default: `final` fields, `List.copyOf` / `Map.copyOf` for
  collections you hand out.
- No swallowed exceptions. Wrap checked exceptions in an unchecked domain
  exception with the cause attached. An empty `catch` needs a comment saying why.
- No `System.out`, `System.err` or `printStackTrace()` outside `main` and tests.
  Log with SLF4J placeholders (`log.info("user {}", id)`), not concatenation.
- Strong-typed identifiers (a record wrapping the value), same reasoning as
  Kotlin and Swift.
- No `new Thread(…)` and no static `ExecutorService`. Inject an `Executor`, or use
  virtual threads on Java 21+.
- `@SuppressWarnings` needs a trailing comment explaining why.

## Build rules

- Gradle: dependencies in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, same as Kotlin.
- Maven: versions live in the parent `<dependencyManagement>` or an imported BOM.
  Module `pom.xml` files declare no `<version>` for managed dependencies.
- No new build plugin without Platform review.

## Testing

- JUnit 5 and AssertJ. Mock only at boundaries you do not own.
- Testcontainers for the real database, not an in-memory stand-in.
- A bug fix lands with a test that fails before the fix.

## Anti-patterns seen in this repo

<!-- FILL IN from your Java style PRs. -->

- Static utility classes holding mutable state.
- `catch (Exception e) { log.error(…) }` and carry on, in a path that should fail.
